slides.title: Early Calculating Devices! 🧮
slides.text: Long before electronic computers, humans invented tools to count! The abacus uses beads on rods for addition and subtraction. Napier's bones uses numbered rods for multiplication. The Pascaline uses gears for mechanical addition!
slides.spoken: Long before electronic computers, humans invented tools to count! The abacus uses beads on rods, Napier's bones multiplies, and the Pascaline uses gears to add.

slides.title: Mechanical & Electromechanical Giants! ⚙️
slides.text: Charles Babbage designed the Difference Engine and the Analytical Engine. The Analytical Engine had input, processing, storage, and output — making Babbage the Father of the Computer! Herman Hollerith built the Tabulating Machine using punched cards.
slides.spoken: Charles Babbage designed the Difference and Analytical Engines, earning the title Father of the Computer. Herman Hollerith built the Tabulating Machine with punched cards.

slides.title: Generations of Computers — 1st & 2nd! ⚡
slides.text: First generation computers (1940s-1950s) used glowing vacuum tubes like ENIAC; they were huge and hot! Second generation (1950s-1960s) replaced tubes with tiny, reliable transistors.
slides.spoken: First generation computers used large vacuum tubes like ENIAC. Second generation replaced tubes with tiny, reliable transistors.

slides.title: Generations — 3rd, 4th & 5th! 💻
slides.text: Third generation introduced Integrated Circuits (ICs). Fourth generation brought microprocessors, creating personal desktop computers! Fifth generation focuses on Artificial Intelligence (AI) to learn and think.
slides.spoken: Third generation used Integrated Circuits. Fourth generation brought microprocessors for personal computers. Fifth generation focuses on Artificial Intelligence.

slides.title: Characteristics & Limitations! 🌟
slides.text: Computers have amazing characteristics: Speed, Accuracy, Storage, Diligence, and Versatility! However, they have limitations: they have no IQ, no feelings, and depend entirely on human instructions and electricity.
slides.spoken: Computers have speed, accuracy, storage, diligence, and versatility. But they have limitations: no IQ, no feelings, and dependence on human instructions.

challenges.question: Which of the following is the OLDEST calculating device among the three early tools?
challenges.hint: Think of the wooden frame with beads sliding on vertical rods used in markets across India!
challenges.misconception: The abacus is the oldest manual counting tool among the three early calculating devices, long predating the Pascaline and the Analytical Engine.

challenges.question: Drag each early device to its correct inventor or origin!
challenges.hint: Abacus has no single inventor (ancient). John Napier invented Napier's bones. Blaise Pascal built the Pascaline.

challenges.question: Who is known as the 'Father of the Computer' for designing the Analytical Engine?
challenges.hint: He designed both the Difference Engine and the Analytical Engine in the 19th century.
challenges.misconception: Charles Babbage is honoured as the father of the computer because his Analytical Engine introduced input, processing, storage, and output.

challenges.question: Drag each Babbage or Hollerith machine to its correct description!
challenges.hint: Difference Engine computed polynomial tables. Analytical Engine was general-purpose. Tabulating Machine used punched cards for census.
challenges.misconception: Remember: Difference Engine computed polynomial tables, Analytical Engine was the first general-purpose design, and Hollerith's machine used punched cards.

easierVariant.hint: Take it slow. Difference Engine computed polynomial tables. Analytical Engine was general-purpose. Tabulating Machine used punched cards for census.

challenges.question: What was the key electronic component of FIRST generation computers like ENIAC?
challenges.hint: They were large glowing glass bulbs that produced a lot of heat and burned out often.
challenges.misconception: First generation computers used vacuum tubes. Transistors came in the second generation, not the first.

challenges.question: Drag each computer generation to its defining technology!
challenges.hint: 1st = Vacuum tubes, 2nd = Transistors, 3rd = Integrated Circuits (IC), 4th = Microprocessors, 5th = Artificial Intelligence.
challenges.misconception: Each generation is defined by its core electronic component: vacuum tubes, transistors, ICs, microprocessors, and AI.

easierVariant.hint: Take it slow. 1st = Vacuum tubes, 2nd = Transistors, 3rd = Integrated Circuits (IC), 4th = Microprocessors, 5th = Artificial Intelligence.
